as: Assamese uses an uncased script. Use modern Assamese punctuation. Danda (।) may mark a natural sentence boundary but is not mandatory; use double danda (॥) only for genuine verse or sectional text.
bn: Bengali uses an uncased script. Use modern Bengali punctuation. Danda (।) may mark a natural sentence boundary but is not mandatory; use double danda (॥) only for genuine verse or sectional text.
gu: Gujarati uses an uncased script. Use conventional modern Gujarati sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
hi: Hindi uses uncased Devanagari. Use modern Hindi punctuation. Danda (।) may mark a natural sentence boundary but is not mandatory; use double danda (॥) only for genuine verse or sectional text.
kn: Kannada uses an uncased script. Use conventional modern Kannada sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
ml: Malayalam uses an uncased script. Use conventional modern Malayalam sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
mr: Marathi uses uncased Devanagari. Use conventional modern Marathi sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
or: Odia uses an uncased script. Use modern Odia punctuation. Danda (।) may mark a natural sentence boundary but is not mandatory; use double danda (॥) only for genuine verse or sectional text.
pa: Punjabi uses uncased Gurmukhi. Use modern Punjabi punctuation. Danda (।) may mark a natural sentence boundary but is not mandatory; use double danda (॥) only for genuine verse or sectional text.
ta: Tamil uses an uncased script. Use conventional modern Tamil sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
te: Telugu uses an uncased script. Use conventional modern Telugu sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
ur: Urdu uses an uncased Arabic-derived script. Prefer Urdu comma (،), semicolon (؛), question mark (؟), and full stop (۔) where natural. Preserve logical Unicode order and never reverse or reshape text; a Western mark may remain appropriate inside a clearly code-switched span.
